giving_subtitle: Connect a Stripe account so this organization can accept donations on its public site.
giving_notConnectedBody: Donations are turned off until this organization has its own Stripe account. Gifts are made directly to you, so the account is yours: your name appears on the donor's bank statement and receipt, and the money lands in your balance without passing through us.
giving_notConnectedNext: Stripe will ask you to verify your organization. Have your EIN and IRS determination letter to hand — it takes about ten minutes, and you can come back to finish later.
giving_status_charges_only: Accepting donations, but payouts are on hold
giving_testModeNotice: This is a test-mode account. No real money can move.
giving_requirementsBody: Your account can't accept donations until these are provided. Continue setup to supply them.
giving_chargesOnlyTitle: Donations are arriving, but payouts are paused
giving_chargesOnlyBody: Gifts are reaching your Stripe balance, but Stripe can't pay them out to your bank yet. This is almost always a bank account that needs re-entering.
giving_walletsNone: No donation domains are registered, so Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link won't appear on your donation form. Set STRIPE_DONATION_DOMAINS and check again.
giving_feesBody: Used to work out what to charge when a donor offers to cover fees. Stripe doesn't publish your negotiated rate, so it has to be entered here.
giving_nonprofitBody: Stripe discounts processing for registered nonprofits where at least 80% of volume is tax-deductible donations. You apply directly and keep the benefit. Have your EIN and IRS determination letter ready, and note that ticket sales and auctions count against that 80%.
giving_receiptBody: Printed on every tax acknowledgment we send your donors. Required for a gift of $250 or more to be substantiated.
giving_legalNameHelp: As registered with the IRS, which may differ from your public name.
giving_acknowledgmentHelp: Leave blank to use the standard "No goods or services were provided in exchange for this contribution."
donations_subtitle: Gifts received through your public site, and the payouts that follow them.
donations_refundBody: This returns money to the donor from your Stripe balance. Stripe's processing fee is not returned — your organization absorbs it either way.
donations_refundQueued: Refund sent to Stripe. This gift will update shortly.
donations_receiptVoidWarning: The donor's tax receipt will be corrected automatically.
donations_payoutsEmpty: No payouts yet. Stripe pays out on the schedule set in your Stripe dashboard.
donations_payoutFailedTitle: A payout to your bank failed
donations_payoutFailedBody: Donations are still arriving, but they can't reach your bank account until this is fixed. Check your bank details in Stripe.
donations_disputeBody: A disputed gift is debited from your Stripe balance straight away. Respond in Stripe — we can't do it for you.
payouts_subtitle: Every transfer Stripe has made to your bank account, and the donations inside each one.
payouts_donationsEmpty: No individual donations are matched to this payout yet.
payouts_pendingBreakdownBody: Stripe hasn't published the itemised breakdown for this payout yet. The net amount is what reached your bank; the donation and fee split will appear once it settles.
payouts_otherNote: Also settles {amount} of refunds, disputes and adjustments.
giving_returnBody: We're checking with Stripe to see where your account stands.
publicSite_donateCoverFeesHint: Adds {amount} so the full gift reaches us.
publicSite_donateError: We couldn't start this gift. Please try again.
publicSite_donateAmountInvalid: Please enter an amount of at least $1.
publicSite_donateEmailRequired: Please enter an email address so we can send your receipt.
publicSite_thanksConfirming: We're confirming your gift. This page will update on its own.
publicSite_thanksConfirmed: Your gift of {amount} has been received. A receipt is on its way to your inbox.
publicSite_thanksProcessing: Your bank transfer is on its way. It can take a few business days to settle, and we'll email your receipt once it does.
publicSite_thanksFailed: That payment didn't go through, so you haven't been charged. Please try again.
error_body: This is usually temporary. Try again in a moment.
error_notFoundBody: That page does not exist, or you may not have access to it.
access_deniedTitle: You do not have access to this page
access_deniedBody: Ask an owner or admin if you think this is a mistake.
access_noCampaignsBody: A team leader works inside assigned campaigns. Ask an owner or admin to assign you one.
dash_subtitle: How the work is going right now.
campaigns_emptyBody: Create a campaign to start tracking work.
campaigns_deleteBody: Deleting {name} also permanently deletes every project in it, and everything attached to those projects. This cannot be undone.
campaigns_slugHelp: Used in public URLs. Suggested from the name; edit before you create.
campaignDetail_mediaBody: The cover image, icon, and promo video shown on this campaign's public page.
campaignDetail_imageUrlHelp: Pasting a URL replaces an uploaded image, and uploading a file replaces a pasted URL — only one can be in effect at a time.
campaignDetail_imageTooLarge: That image is larger than 10 MB
campaignDetail_slugLocked: The public URL — /{slug}. Frozen once created so links never break.
campaignDetail_membersEnabledHelp: Allow projects in this campaign to have members.
campaignDetail_tripsEnabledHelp: Plan trips for this campaign — travellers, flights, readiness and costs. Off unless you turn it on.
campaignDetail_summaryPlaceholder: A short description of this campaign (optional)
campaignDetail_storyPlaceholder: The longer public story of this campaign (optional)
campaignDetail_isPublishedHelp: Make this campaign visible on the public site.
campaignDetail_publicBody: How this campaign appears on your public site.
members_subtitle: Who can use the admin app, and what they may do.
members_assignHelp: A team leader only works in the campaigns assigned here.
members_inviteHelp: Invitations are sent from the organization profile.
projects_emptyBody: Create the first record to get started.
projects_notFound: That record could not be found
money_subtitle: Every transaction and where it was attributed.
settings_perAttendeeHelp: A per-traveller item becomes one task for each person going, assigned to them. Everything else is one task for the whole trip.
settings_perAttendeeMoneyHelp: A per-traveller amount is multiplied by the number of people going. Airfare is quoted per seat; a van rental is not.
settings_scopeTripHelp: The checklist every new trip in this campaign starts with. Items marked per traveller become one task for each person going.
settings_stageKeyHelp: Permanent. Used by projects, documents and the public site.
settings_stageDefaultHelp: Where new records start. Exactly one per campaign.
settings_stageFundedGateHelp: Marks a record fully funded. Exactly one per campaign.
settings_stageSystemLocked: System stages are part of the campaign and cannot be deleted.
settings_stageDeleteBody: Deleting {label} cannot be undone. A stage that still has records in it cannot be deleted.
settings_tripBudgetDeleteBody: Trips built from it keep their budget — the lines were copied, not linked. Only the preset goes.
settings_tripBudgetEmptyBody: A preset saves typing the same airfare, lodging and ground transport lines into every trip.
settings_tripBudgetHelp: Named sets of budget lines a new trip can start from. Applying one copies its lines onto the trip, so editing a preset later never changes a trip already built from it.
settings_appendOnlyNote: Versions are append-only. Publish a new version instead of editing an old one — existing budgets keep the version they snapshotted.
settings_amountsInDollars: Enter dollars, e.g. 1250.00. Stored to the cent.
settings_amountInvalid: Amounts must be a whole number of cents.
settings_categoryDeleteBody: Deleting {name} does not delete its fields — they become uncategorized.
settings_fieldKeyHelp: Permanent. Values are stored under this key on every record.
settings_fieldPublicWarning: Public fields are shown on your public site to anyone who visits.
settings_fieldPublicConfirmBody: Every value already stored in this field becomes visible on your public site.
settings_fieldDeleteBody: Deleting {label} removes the field everywhere. Values already stored on records are left behind.
settings_scopeInheritHelp: A campaign inherits every org-wide field on top of its own.
settings_lineItemKeyDuplicate: Each line item needs its own key.
settings_taskItemKeyDuplicate: Each item needs its own key.
settings_stageDefaultLocked: The default stage cannot be deleted — mark another stage as default first.
money_deleteTransactionBody: This removes the transaction and every allocation attributing it. The amount will no longer appear in totals.
money_amountInvalid: Enter a whole number of cents, for example 12.34
projects_deleteBody: This removes the record, its budget and its documents. Money already recorded keeps its amount and loses only its attribution.
projects_removeMemberBody: This removes the person from this record. The contact itself is not deleted, and stays available to add elsewhere.
updates_bodyHint: Type / to add a heading, a list, a photo or a video. What you see here is how it will look once published.
updates_saveFailed: We could not save that. Try again.
updates_publishFailed: We could not publish that. Try again.
updates_deleteConfirm: Delete this update? Its photos are deleted with it, and that is the only way to take a published photo back.
updates_deleteFailed: We could not delete that. Try again.
updates_emptyPublic: No updates have been shared yet.
updates_cannotPublish: You can write and edit updates. Someone with publishing rights reviews and publishes them.
updates_videoPrompt: Paste a YouTube or Vimeo link
updates_imageTooLarge: That image is too large. The limit is 10 MB.
projects_publicNameHelp: What the public site may call this record. Never derived from the real name.
projects_internalOnly: Internal only — never shown on the public site
projects_budgetDeleteBody: This removes the budget and its target. Money already attributed to this record is untouched.
projects_documentDeleteBody: This removes the document and any uploaded file with it. This cannot be undone.
contacts_deleteBody: This removes the contact. Donations they gave keep their amount and lose only the donor name.
households_deleteBody: This removes the household. The people in it are not deleted.
org_settingsBody: How this organization is named on public pages, and what it calls its campaigns.
org_slugHelp: The unique handle public pages are served under. Required before any public page works.
publicSiteSettings_subtitle: Manage your public identity, address, theme, and custom domains.
publicSiteSettings_identityBody: The name and tagline shown on your public site.
publicSiteSettings_publicNameHelp: Shown as the wordmark on your public site. Falls back to your organization's name when left blank.
publicSiteSettings_taglineHelp: A short line shown in your public site's footer.
publicSiteSettings_addressBody: The web address your public site is served from.
publicSiteSettings_addressLiveAt: Your public site is live at {address}.
publicSiteSettings_addressChoose: Choose an address to publish your public site.
publicSiteSettings_themeBody: The color theme applied to your public site.
publicSiteSettings_domainsBody: Point your own domain at your public site. Verify ownership with a DNS record.
publicSiteSettings_domainsNotice: Custom domains aren't available yet — this is a preview of the layout, not a working form.
campaignContacts_subtitle: Everyone taking part in this campaign.
campaignContacts_emptyBody: Add someone who already exists, or create a new person.
campaignContacts_removeBody: This removes them from this campaign only. The contact stays in your organization.
campaignContacts_alreadyIn: Everyone already belongs to this campaign
contactDetail_notFound: That contact could not be found
contactDetail_noCustomFields: No custom fields defined. Add them in Settings.
contactDetail_missingRequired: Fill in the required fields first
contactDetail_noDonations: No donations attributed to this person yet. Attribute one when recording a donation.
contactDetail_firstNameHelp: The name this person actually goes by.
contactDetail_givenNameHelp: Their formal name, if it differs from the preferred first name above.
contactDetail_publicFirstNameHelp: Shown on public pages instead of the name above. Leave blank to keep this person's name private.
contactDetail_blockedHelp: Bounced or unsubscribed. Excluded from sends.
contactDetail_removeEmailBody: This removes the email from this contact.
contactDetail_removePhoneBody: This removes the phone number from this contact.
contactDetail_removeAddressBody: This removes the address from this contact.
contactDetail_removeBackgroundCheckBody: This removes the background check record.
households_removeMemberBody: This removes them from the household. The contact itself is not deleted, and stays available to add elsewhere.
projectDetail_photoTooLarge: That image is larger than 10 MB
projectDetail_stageConfirmBody: The stage is an admin-set status. Moving it does not change whether this record is published.
projectDetail_internalHelp: None of this may leave the app. A site reference identifies where a family was held, and a phone number is their lifeline.
projectDetail_publishLabel: Show on the public donor site
projectDetail_publishHelp: Publishing is independent of the pipeline stage.
projectDetail_linkNotLive: This link only works once the record is published.
projectDetail_whatDonorsSeeBody: The public name if one is set, the story, the photo and funding progress. Never the full name, address, phone, site reference or any donor details.
projectDetail_publicNameHelp: Shown instead of the real name. Left empty, the record shows only its number.
projectDetail_noDonations: No donations attributed to this record yet. Attribute one when recording a donation.
projectDetail_noInternalFields: No internal fields defined for this campaign yet
projectDetail_noInternalFieldsBody: Add custom fields in Settings and leave them not public. They will appear here and never reach the public site.
projectDetail_internalFieldsHelp: These are this campaign's own fields, marked not public. Nothing here reaches the public site.
money_budgetItemHelp: Untagged spend lands in the budget's Unassigned row
projects_spendIntro: Records a real expenditure from this record's fund, tagged to this budget line. It rolls up into the line's Actual and appears in Budget alongside every other transaction.
projects_spendReceiptHelp: Optional but recommended — stored privately as proof of this expenditure.
projects_spendReceiptTooLarge: That receipt is larger than 10 MB
projects_spendAmountInvalid: Enter a positive dollar amount, for example 150.00
projects_donationIntro: Records money received for this record. It counts toward Raised on this record and appears in Giving alongside every other gift.
projects_donationDonorHelp: Optional — leave it on "No donor recorded" for an anonymous gift.
projects_donationReceiptHelp: Optional — stored privately as proof of this gift.
projects_donationReceiptTooLarge: That receipt is larger than 10 MB
projects_donationAmountInvalid: Enter a positive dollar amount, for example 150.00
projects_documentLedgerHint: Recorded with a donation or an expenditure. Manage it from the money ledger.
publicSite_accountSignOutFailed: We couldn't sign you out. Please try again.
publicSite_loginSubtitle: We'll email you a link to sign in — there's no password to remember.
publicSite_privacyNote: For the privacy of those we serve, we share stories and photos only with consent, and never publish locations or full names.
publicSite_fundingGoalMetSentence: This {object} is {goal}. Thank you to everyone who made it happen.
publicSite_fundingFundedExtraSentence: Fully funded — every extra gift helps the next {object}.
publicSite_fundingRemainingSentence: {amount} to go until this {object} is fully funded.
publicSite_storyPending: Their story is being written — check back soon.
publicSite_interestAmountPlaceholder: Any amount helps — or leave blank
publicSite_interestMessagePlaceholder: Anything you would like us to know
publicSite_interestClosedNotice: Enquiries aren't open yet — our team is still setting this up. Please check back soon.
publicSite_interestNoPayment: No payment happens on this page. Once enquiries open, our team will reach out personally to talk through the next step.
publicSite_orgEmptyBody: This site's campaigns aren't live yet. Please check back soon.
publicSite_gridEmptyBody: We publish each profile as soon as it is safe to share. Check back soon.
publicSite_donateCoverFees: Add a little to cover processing fees
publicSite_donateClosedNotice: Online giving isn't connected yet — our team is still setting this up. Please check back soon.
publicSite_donateSecureNote: Card details are entered on Stripe's secure checkout, never on this page.
campaignEmbed_body: Paste a snippet into your website and it stays in sync with this campaign — no second copy of the data to maintain.
campaignEmbed_recordHint: Replace {number} with the record you want to show.
campaignEmbed_scriptNote: Include the script once per page, however many widgets you embed.
campaignEmbed_unpublished: Publish this campaign before embedding it — the widgets show nothing until then.
campaignEmbed_noSlug: Set your site address on the Public site settings page before embedding.
settings_impactTagHelp: An impact tag turns an item into a stat. Leave it blank for ordinary operational work. Items sharing a tag are one number, counted once per record — so the Public and Dash switches belong to the tag and move together.
settings_taskPublicWarning: A stat set to show on the public site publishes a count of the records that completed it. Anyone visiting your public site can see that number.
settings_stageCountsTowardImpactHelp: Off for a stage that means the record should never have been here. A record that left the programme successfully should stay on.
campaignStats_body: The numbers this campaign publishes, in this order. Each can go on your public site, your dashboard, or both.
campaignStats_empty: No stats selected — your public site shows none.
campaignStats_issueSmallCount: Hidden on your public site: fewer than 5 records. Small counts can identify someone.
campaignStats_issueSmallBucket: Hidden on your public site: one of this field's answers has fewer than 5 records, and publishing the rest would still give away how rare it is.
campaignStats_issuePrivateField: Hidden on your public site: that field isn't public. Mark it public in Custom fields first.
campaignStats_issueProtectedKey: That field can never be published — its key is one that could identify where someone was held.
campaignStats_issueUnknownMetric: That built-in number no longer exists.
dashStats_body: Your campaign's own numbers, including the ones you keep internal.
dashStats_empty: No stats are set to show here. Add one under Settings → Public site.
dashStats_lifetime: All time — this one has no date to filter on
orgStats_body: Which campaigns show their numbers on your organisation's home page. Each gets its own section — nothing is added together, because campaigns measure different things.
orgStats_empty: No sections — your home page shows no numbers.
tasks_body: The steps this campaign's checklist defines for a record.
tasks_emptyBody: Add the items from your campaign's active checklist to get started.
tasks_noTemplateBody: This campaign has no active task template. Create one under Settings → Task templates.
tasks_filteredEmptyBody: {done} of {total} items are done. Choose another status above to see them.
settings_taskAppendOnlyNote: A new version is how a checklist changes over time. You can also edit an existing version in place — records already working through it keep the wording they started with.
settings_taskEditNote: Editing this version changes what future records are given. Items already added to a record keep the label, tag and public setting they were created with.
settings_taskItemKeyLocked: Permanent once saved — records match their checklist to the template by this key.
settings_taskItemRemovedKeepsTasks: Records already working through these keep them: {items}. Removing an item stops it being offered to new records; it does not erase work already done.
campaignStats_willBeCalled: Will be called “{label}” — you can rename it after adding.
campaignStats_kindBuiltin: A number the app already tracks
campaignStats_kindBuiltinHelp: Records that met their goal, people reached, money raised. Nothing to set up — pick one and it starts counting.
campaignStats_kindFieldHelp: Any field you've defined on a record — total it up, or count how many records have a value.
campaignStats_kindTaskHelp: Counts records where a tagged checklist item is ticked. Add the tag on a checklist version below first.
campaignStats_kindMemberHelp: Counts people rather than records — how many children were enrolled in school, not how many families enrolled one.
campaignStats_aggregateCount: How many records have a value
campaignStats_allAdded: Every built-in number is already on the list.
campaignStats_noFields: No custom fields yet — add one under Custom fields.
campaignStats_noTags: No checklist tags yet — tag an item on a checklist version below.
privacy_body: How cautious your public site is with small numbers and sensitive field names. The defaults suit an organisation whose records are people.
privacy_thresholdHelp: A published count smaller than this is withheld. Small counts can identify someone — “1 record” next to a handful of published profiles gives them away.
privacy_thresholdInvalid: Enter a whole number, 0 or more.
privacy_thresholdOffWarning: Set to 0, no count is ever withheld. Reasonable if your records are wells or deliveries. If they are people, a count of 1 or 2 can identify them.
privacy_extraKeys: Also never publish these field keys
privacy_extraKeysHelp: One per line. Use this for anything sensitive in your own work that the shared list wouldn't guess. A field with one of these keys can never be marked public.
privacy_patternKeys: anything containing phone, address or location, or ending in _ref
taskList_viewSaveBody: The filters and sort you are looking at now are stored as a link you can come back to.
taskList_viewShareHelp: Everyone in the organisation can apply a shared view. They still only ever see the tasks they are allowed to see.
taskList_viewDeleteBody: This deletes the saved view “{name}”. The tasks it filtered are untouched.
taskList_subtitle: Everything this campaign is tracking — checklist steps and the work around them.
taskList_adminSubtitle: Every task in the organisation, across all campaigns.
taskList_pickCampaignToAdd: Choose a campaign above to add a task.
taskList_contactsTruncated: Showing the first contacts only. Search on the contacts page to find the rest.
taskList_facetsTruncated: There are too many tasks to check every one, so a rarely used value may be missing from the filters above.
taskList_truncated: There are more tasks than this list loads. The ones it left out are not on a later page either — narrow the filters to bring them in.
taskList_emptyBody: Add one here, or give a record its campaign checklist.
taskList_noMatchBody: Clear the filters to see the rest of the list.
taskList_bulkTooMany: Select at most {max} tasks at a time.
taskList_bulkCompleteBody: {count} of the tasks you selected count toward numbers on your public site: {stats}. Completing them raises those numbers.
taskList_deleteBody: This deletes “{label}”. It cannot be undone.
taskList_deletePublicBody: This deletes “{label}”. It is completed and counts toward “{stat}”, so deleting it reduces a number on your public site. It cannot be undone.
taskSheet_projectPinned: This task belongs to the record you are looking at. Move it from the Tasks page if it needs to live somewhere else.
taskSheet_impactTagNeedsProject: An impact tag needs a record. Impact stats count distinct records, so a tagged campaign-level task would count zero forever.
taskSheet_impactTagPublic: This tag feeds a number on your public site.
taskSheet_templateReadonly: This step comes from the campaign checklist. Its title, key and impact tag are the same on every record that carries it — edit the template to change them.
taskSheet_discardBody: This task has edits you have not saved. Closing now loses them.
portal_greetingSubtitle: Everything here is yours — your giving, the stories you are part of, and anything waiting on you.
portal_noAccessBody: You're signed in, but this account isn't connected to anyone here. If you have an invitation, it was probably sent to a different email address than the one below.
portal_noAccessInvitedBody: We've invited this address but it hasn't been taken up yet. Open the link in that email to finish, or ask us to send it again.
portal_noAccessRevokedTitle: This account no longer has access
portal_noAccessRevokedBody: Your portal access has ended. Your records and your giving are untouched — get in touch if you think this is a mistake.
portal_noAccessSwitchAccount: Sign out and use a different account
portal_noAccessHelp: Still stuck? Reply to the email that brought you here and we'll sort it out.
portal_givingSubtitle: Every gift you have made, and where it went.
portal_givingTruncated: Showing your most recent gifts. Ask us if you need the full history.
portal_recordsSubtitle: The people and projects your support and your involvement connect you to.
portal_recordsEmpty: Nothing is connected to you yet.
portal_recordNotFound: That story is not one of yours.
portal_ownRecordNote: This is your own record, shown to you as it really reads.
portal_tasksSubtitle: Anything we have asked of you that is still open.
portal_tasksTruncated: Some tasks may not be shown. Tell us if something you expected is missing.
portal_profileSubtitle: Keep these current so we can reach you. Ask us if a name needs changing.
portal_profileSaveFailed: We could not save that. Try again.
portal_profileFixedNote: Your name and email are how we recognise you. Ask us to change either.
portal_profileUpdateDetail: How much you'd like to hear
portal_profilePreferredContact: How you'd like to be reached
portal_tripAddFlightHelp: Times are local to each airport — enter them exactly as they appear on your ticket.
portal_tripNoFlights: No flights have been added yet.
portal_tripNotFoundBody: This trip either does not exist or you are not travelling on it.
portal_tripsEmptyBody: When you are added to a trip, its dates and itinerary will appear here.
portal_tripsSubtitle: Your dates, your flights, and who else is going.
contactDetail_portalInviteFailed: We could not send that invitation.
contactDetail_portalNeedsEmail: Add an email address before inviting this person to the portal.
contactDetail_revokePortalBody: They will be signed out of the portal at once. Their record, their giving and their history all stay.
trips_subtitle: Where this campaign is going, and who is going with it.
trips_deleteBody: This removes the trip, its roster, its flights, its planned costs and its checklist items. The people and records it touched are not deleted.
trips_notFound: That trip could not be found
trips_emptyBody: Plan the first trip for this campaign to get started.
trips_countryCodeHelp: Two letters, for grouping only. Optional.
trips_nameHelp: Prefilled from the campaign, the record and the departure date. Edit it freely — it stays yours from here on.
trips_projectHelp: Optional. Picking one seeds the trip name and links the first record; you can add more on the trip page afterwards.
tripDetail_itineraryBody: Every leg as the ticket prints it. Times are local to their own airport.
tripDetail_noSegmentsBody: Add one row per leg — Dallas to Doha and Doha to Islamabad are two.
tripDetail_removeSegmentBody: This removes the leg from the itinerary. Nothing else on the trip changes.
tripDetail_timeHelp: Local time at the airport, exactly as the boarding pass reads it.
tripDetail_zoneHelp: An IANA name such as America/Chicago. Optional — without it the flight still shows, and durations stay hidden rather than guessed.
tripDetail_missingZone: Add a timezone to each leg to see how long it takes.
tripDetail_attendingBody: The organisation's own people. Adding someone here does not add them to any record this trip visits.
tripDetail_noAttendeesBody: Add the people going, then their flights and checklist items follow.
tripDetail_flightsCopied: {count} legs copied — edit the ones that differ
tripDetail_removeAttendeeBody: This takes the person off this trip, along with any flights entered for them alone. The contact itself is not deleted.
tripDetail_checklistBody: What has to be true before this trip can board. Items are ticked, never filled in — no passport or visa numbers are stored.
tripDetail_checklistEmptyBody: Add the items from your campaign's trip checklist to get started.
tripDetail_noTemplateBody: This campaign has no active trip checklist. Create one under Settings → Task templates.
tripDetail_removeLineBody: This removes the planned line. Money already recorded is untouched.
tripDetail_linePerAttendeeHelp: The amount is quoted per seat, and the line total is the amount times the confirmed roster.
tripDetail_confirmedRoster: Per-person lines are multiplied by {count} confirmed travellers.
tripDetail_noLinesBody: Add what this trip expects to spend — airfare, lodging, ground transport, visas.
tripDetail_actualsEmptyBody: Trip spending is attributed in the ledger. This panel fills in once that attribution lands; nothing is missing from your books in the meantime.
tripDetail_projectsBody: The records this trip visits. Each links through to its own page.
tripDetail_noProjectsBody: A trip may exist before anyone has decided which records it reaches.
tripDetail_unlinkProjectBody: This removes the link only. The record and the trip both survive it.
memberSides_subtitle: People on a record who look like your own team, and what the published numbers become if you say so.
memberSides_intro: Everyone on a record counts as someone that record reached until they are marked as team. These rows have roles that read like your own staff and volunteers, so they may be inflating what you publish.
memberSides_heuristicNote: This is a guess made from the role text, and it can be wrong in both directions — it misses vocabulary it has never seen, and it may flag someone you really do serve. Nothing changes until you confirm it.
memberSides_nothingBody: No record has a person on it whose role reads like your own team. Nothing here is inflating a published number.
memberSides_selectCampaignBody: Corrections are made one campaign at a time, so you see that campaign's numbers before you decide.
memberSides_rowsBody: Untick anyone this campaign really does serve. The numbers below follow whatever is ticked.
memberSides_impactBody: Before and after, computed the same way this campaign's own stats are. Only the numbers that move are listed.
memberSides_impactNoneBody: Nothing this campaign publishes counts these people, so marking them as team changes no figure here.
memberSides_householdsBody: A record's public page publishes how many people are on it, and names those with a public first name. These are the records that changes.
memberSides_confirmBody: This changes numbers your donors may already have seen, and it is not undone from this screen — a row is corrected afterwards on the record itself.
memberSides_appliedNothing: Everyone you picked was already marked as team
checkins_noSelectionBody: Choose a check-in on the left to read its transcript and the decisions behind it.
checkins_notConfiguredBody: No Anthropic API key is set on this deployment. Messages you write yourself still work; a check-in will open and then fail its first turn.
reviewReason_draft_failed: Drafting did not return a draft
checkinDetail_noMessagesBody: The opening message is written by the responder and appears here once it runs.
checkinDetail_draftReady: A draft update is waiting for review
checkinDetail_draftReadyBody: Nothing has been published. Read it on the record's updates, edit it, and decide there.
checkinDetail_closeBody: Mark this conversation finished. It cannot be reopened — a person has said things the engine does not know about.
checkinDetail_deleteBody: Deletes the transcript, every model call, and every rating. Any draft it produced is kept. This cannot be undone.
checkinDetail_simulateTitle: Record a reply from the family
checkinDetail_simulateBody: WhatsApp delivery is not built yet, so a reply that arrived some other way is entered here. This is stored as the family's own words and is scanned for anything that needs a person before it reaches a model.
checkinDetail_simulateEscalated: Recorded, and handed to a person
checkinDetail_simulateClosed: This check-in is closed to the engine. A reply is still stored, but nothing further is asked.
checkinDetail_fromUsPerson: Sent to the family, written by a person
checkinDetail_fromUsEngine: Sent to the family, written by the engine
checkinCompose_disabledCheckin: The engine is running this check-in and is mid-conversation. Close the check-in before writing to this family yourself.
checkinObjectives_body: Frozen when the conversation opened, so a later change to the default set cannot rewrite what was asked.
checkinTrace_body: What was sent, what came back, and which prompt version produced it. This is the audit trail.
escalation_body: A reply from this family matched a phrase that stops the conversation. Nothing further has been asked, and no draft will be written.
escalation_resolveBody: Say what was done. This note is the record of how the charity responded.
checkinStart_body: Opens a conversation with this family and writes the first message. Nothing is sent until the transport is connected.
checkinStart_contactHelp: The person on this record who holds the phone. Optional — the conversation can be opened before that is decided.
checkinStart_localeHelp: Only English and Spanish replies can be scanned for anything that needs a person.
checkinPrompts_subtitle: Append-only. A wording change is a new version, never an edit.
checkinPrompts_seedNone: Every shipped version is already here
checkinPrompts_newBody: This is inserted inactive. Replay real conversations against it before putting it in front of a family.
checkinPrompts_versionHelp: A name that will never be reused, such as responder-2.
checkinPrompts_modelHelp: The model this wording was tuned for. The same words behave differently on a different tier.
checkinPrompts_emptyBody: Seed the shipped set to start.
messages_subtitle: Conversations with families, and the trace behind every one.
messages_newBody: Nothing is delivered yet — WhatsApp is not connected, so what gets written is held here for a person to send.
messages_kindCheckinHelp: Asks about work, school, the children and how the family is doing; reads each reply, stops once it has what it needs, and drafts an update for someone to review. Anything worrying in a reply stops it and hands over to a person.
messages_emptyBody: Start a conversation with a family and it appears here.
messages_kindDirectHelp: A plain conversation with someone in this campaign. You write every message yourself and replies are recorded against it; no model is ever called, and anything worrying in a reply still stops the thread and hands over to a person.
messages_recipientPlaceholder: Choose a record or a person
messages_recipientHelp: Anyone in this campaign: a family's record, or a person on a record, a trip, or the campaign itself.
messages_recipientCheckinHelp: A check-in asks about a household, so it can only be opened on a record.
checkinTemplates_subtitle: The steps a check-in works through, and what each answer does. Versions are append-only; promoting one changes what the next check-in asks, never a conversation already open.
checkinTemplates_noneBody: Until one is active, check-ins ask the four objectives this build ships with.
checkinTemplates_seeded: Default template and update format added.
checkinTemplates_entryMessage: Guidance while this step is open (optional)
checkinTemplates_objectiveDescription: What a satisfying answer looks like
checkinTemplates_objectiveDescriptionHel: The only text the judge sees. Describe the answer, not the question.
checkinTemplates_captureNone: Just capture it for the update
checkinTemplates_skipIfKnown: Skip if the record already has a value
checkinFormats_subtitle: The sections a drafted update is made of. These become the tool the drafting model must fill in, so a section here is a section the draft will have.
checkinFormats_noneBody: Until one is active, drafts come back as a title and one block of prose.
checkinFormats_instructionsHelp: Tone and rules that are not structural. Added to the drafter's brief, not to the prompt that protects the family.
checkinFormats_oneSectionNote: A single section produces no heading — just prose, the way updates read today.
workflows_subtitle: A workflow is a configured agent: what it asks, what it files, how it speaks, and what shape its report takes.
workflows_newBody: It starts as a draft, seeded with the shipped objectives, report and prompts. Nothing runs under it until you publish.
workflows_emptyBody: Nothing is configured to talk to anyone. Start one and it opens as a draft you can edit freely.
workflows_needCampaign: A workflow runs against a campaign's records, so create a campaign first.
workflows_archiveBody: It leaves the pickers and starts nothing new. Its published versions are kept, so every run that names one stays replayable.
workflows_deleteBody: It has never been published, so nothing has ever run under it and there is no record to keep. This cannot be undone.
workflows_problemKey: Every step, objective and section needs a key: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
workflows_problemDuplicate: Two objectives or two sections share a key. A rating would land on whichever the engine indexed last.
workflows_stepsEmptyBody: A step is a named group of objectives with one lead-in. Every step runs; the grouping is for you, not for the engine.
workflows_stepEntryMessageHelp: Context for the responder while any objective in this step is open. Guidance, never a script — a verbatim line is how a warm message becomes a form.
workflows_objectiveKeyHelp: Stable and never reused. Ratings and captured answers are filed under it.
workflows_objectiveLabelHelp: Admin-facing. Never sent to a model.
workflows_objectiveDescription: What a satisfying answer looks like
workflows_objectiveDescriptionHelp: The only text the judge sees about this objective. Describe the answer, not the question — there is no family profile behind it.
workflows_requiresHelp: Facts read off the record. Nothing ticked means the objective always applies. This asks whether the question fits the household — not whether we were already told.
workflows_captureNoFields: No fields are defined for this entity yet.
workflows_skipIfKnown: Do not ask when the record already holds the answer
workflows_defaultHint: Blank uses the engine default of {value}.
workflows_maxAttemptsHelp: Blank means no cap of its own. The conversation still stops after {count} turns.
workflows_report_body: What a finished run writes. Each section becomes a required field on the drafting tool, so the shape is enforced rather than requested.
workflows_titleGuidanceHelp: Handed to the drafter as the description of the title field.
workflows_instructionsHelp: Tone and style that is not structural. What the drafter may say about a family lives in its prompt, on the Voice tab.
workflows_sectionsBody: Every section is required. A section that can be empty should say so in its own guidance and let the draft say “nothing to report”.
workflows_sectionKeyHelp: Lowercase snake_case. Becomes a property on the drafting tool.
workflows_sectionLabelHelp: The heading in the assembled update. A one-section report produces no heading at all.
workflows_sectionGuidanceHelp: Handed to the drafter as this section's description.
workflows_roleHelp_responder: The only voice a family reads. It is told how to ask, never given the questions verbatim.
workflows_roleHelp_judge: Reads the latest turns and rates each objective. It is never shown the family profile.
workflows_roleHelp_drafter: Turns a finished conversation into a draft for a member of staff. It has no tool that could publish anything.
workflows_promptModelHelp: The model this wording was tuned for. The same words behave differently on a different tier.
workflows_trigger_body: Whatever starts it, the same guard applies: one open run per record, and a run needs a record to be about.
workflows_trigger_manualHelp: A member of staff starts it on a record.
workflows_trigger_stageChangeHelp: Starts when a record enters the chosen pipeline stage.
workflows_trigger_scheduleHelp: Every so many months, per record.
workflows_trigger_noStages: This campaign has no pipeline stages to trigger on.
workflows_trigger_scheduleNote: Stored, but nothing runs it yet — the schedule is deferred until the transport exists.
workflows_problemNoObjectives: A workflow needs at least one objective before it can be published.
workflows_problemNoSections: A report needs at least one section before it can be published.
workflows_problemReservedSection: A section cannot be called “title” — that is the drafting tool’s own field.
